##### What does Micro Tolerance Load Regulation mean?

It refers to how closely the PSU keeps its output voltage within the target range as system load changes. On PRIME TX ATX 3.1, load regulation is specified at under 0.5%. This does not mean the PC will automatically run faster, but it is part of the PSU's electrical performance and voltage stability.

##### Is PRIME TX only meant for gaming PCs?

No. The 1300 W and 1600 W models can also make sense for content creation or professional workstations with high power requirements. The important point is to choose the PSU according to the complete system rather than the GPU alone. For a very demanding workstation, it is also worth checking the number and type of GPU power connections required.

##### What changed when PRIME TX moved from ATX 3.0 to ATX 3.1?

Earlier versions of this platform were originally released under ATX 3.0 and shipped with 12VHPWR cables. The current ATX 3.1 models use the revised 12V-2×6 connector instead. If you want to compare other Seasonic models using the current standard, you can browse our ATX 3.1 and PCIe 5.1 power supplies.

## Capacities and rails

Seasonic's specification table is written for the 1600 W model and shows 25 A on the +3.3 V rail, 25 A on the +5 V rail, 133.3 A on the +12 V rail, 0.5 A on the -12 V rail and 3 A on the +5 V standby output. The maximum power figures are 125 W for the combined 3.3 V and 5 V rails, 1600 W for the 12 V rail, 6 W for -12 V and 15 W for standby. The total continuous power is listed as 1600 W at 115 to 240 V AC for the larger model and 1300 W at 100 to 240 V AC for the smaller model, and the AC input current is 15 to 10 A at 50 to 60 Hz. The distinction between 115 V and 100 V input for the two versions is a practical detail to check if you plan to run the unit in a region with lower mains voltage. As with most modern supplies, essentially all of the capacity sits on the 12 V rail, where processors and graphics cards draw their power. For help judging how much capacity a system actually needs, our guide on how much PSU wattage you need is a good starting point, because a 1300 W or 1600 W unit is aimed at very demanding configurations.

...

## ATX 3.1 and the 12V-2x6 connectors

The PRIME TX ATX 3.1 is described as ATX 3.1 and PCIe 5.1 ready, and both capacities are equipped with native 12V-2x6 connectors. Seasonic explains that earlier versions of this platform were released under ATX 3.0 and shipped with 12VHPWR cables, and that the current models use the revised 12V-2x6 connector instead. The cable table lists a 700 mm 12V-2x6 cable with a 12+4-pin connector at each end, two of them for the 1600 W model and one for the 1300 W model. Seasonic gives a specific installation warning: both 12V-2x6 connectors of the cable must always be plugged into the power supply and the graphics card, fully inserted, click-locked and tight, and the cable should not be bent or forced after it is plugged in. Read our explainer on the 12VHPWR connector for the background to that advice.

...

The fan is 135 mm with a fluid dynamic bearing, controlled by the digital hybrid system, and the listed life expectancy is 50,000 hours at 40 degrees Celsius and 15 to 65 percent relative humidity. Seasonic's page explains that fluid dynamic bearings use oil to absorb impact and lubricate the shaft, which reduces friction and vibration and, in the company's words, makes them extremely reliable and quieter than ball-bearing fans. The Cybenetics noise level is Lambda A. The operating temperature is 0 to 50 degrees Celsius and the MTBF is 100,000 hours at 25 degrees Celsius excluding the fan. The housing measures 210 by 150 by 86 mm, and Seasonic itself points out that ATX power supplies vary in depth and that drive cages or limited cable-routing space can reduce the room available in some cases, so the length needs to be checked against the case before purchase.

...

## Protection and certification

Listed protections are over-power, over-voltage, under-voltage, over-current, over-temperature and short-circuit protection, and the input is full range. Safety and EMC certifications include cTUVus, TUV, CB, CCC, BSMI, EAC and CE, and the environmental compliance list names RoHS, WEEE, ErP Lot 6 and REACH. Seasonic offers a datasheet, quick installation guide and user manual as downloads. Its FAQ notes that the 1300 W and 1600 W models can make sense for content creation or professional workstations as well as gaming PCs, but that the supply should be chosen by the complete system, including the number and type of GPU power connections.

Seasonic’s new Prime TX ATX 3.1 range is an update of the previous ATX 3.0 range. In fact, nothing has changed except the 12VHPWR connector, which has been upgraded to the 12V-2×6 standard. Power ratings remain the same at 1300W and 1600W for prices ranging from €442.99 to €494.99, with even a Noctua edition at €499.

Let’s start with the dimensions of this Seasonic Prime TX-1300. Here we have a premium power supply with a certain footprint. These new 1300 W and 1600 W models are the same size. The width is 150 mm, the depth 210 mm and the height 86 mm. It should therefore fit comfortably into most modern ATX cases. The weight should also be taken into account: we’re talking about 3 kg on the scale.

...

The design remains unchanged from that of the 2022 range. The fan is 135 mm with 11 blades. It is rarely activated, even with loads of over an hour between 500 and 700 W.

The front of the power supply remains classic. There’s the IEC C19 connector for connecting the power cord, a button for activating the fan’s hybrid mode, and a power switch. In terms of design, there’s nothing to suggest a high-end power supply, apart from the C19 connector.

...

As far as the electrics are concerned, this 1300W Prime TX-1300 features a single 12V rail. This rail is capable of delivering 1300 W at 108 A. The internal design is of the highest quality, based on reliable, tried-and-tested components. We can’t wait to put this model through its paces on the test bench and in overclocking sessions.

The other rails are rated at 25 A for 3.3 V and 5 V. In terms of combined power, that’s 125 W, enough to calmly power all the machine’s peripherals: SSD, HDD, USB and so on. Finally, we’d like to mention the -12 V 0.5 A (6 W) and 5 VsB 3 A (15 W) rails.
